analysis:
This PR adds add-on hold load fences (addonHoldLoadRefusal) at several points in the model-load paths. I examined the Nemotron Super patch and base/head text (ProviderLoop+NemotronSuper.swift head lines 46 and 170), the NativeMiMo head tail (lines 522-676, which the patch places at line ~251), and the ModelLoading patch excerpt. The new checks are fail-closed refusals that throw before GPU/weight allocation (before requireMetal and the reslice gate at line 46-50) and again before slot publication at line 170. They sit before `throwIfRetiring`, `engineV2Runtime.register` and `modelSlots` assignment, so no slot is published on refusal. In publishNemotronSuperSlot, a throw leaves the owner unpublished. The caller installNemotronSuperSlot (line 123) retires the owner via retireUnpublishedNemotronSuper and restores the reslice, so the new throw reuses the existing cleanup path used for CancellationError. The release of the reslice gate is handled in the loadNemotronSuperSlot catch at line 55. The added error does not expose paths or payload data: nemotronSuperLoadFailure records the message only for InferenceError.modelLoadFailed. The refusal type is unseen, and if it is not an InferenceError, it maps to the generic 'native construction was refused' reason. That affects diagnostics only, not security.

T-059 (TB-012) is the relevant threat. The change is a mitigation that prevents loading models beside running VMs. Remaining unverified items: the definition of addonHoldLoadRefusal and modelLoadInterruption in files not supplied; the truncated ModelLoading patch (lines 938-948 and 1041-1048 are not visible); and the NativeMiMo head excerpt showing only the retirement tail, not the changed line 251. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a regression. No change touches encryption, attestation, authorization or the coordinator wire. Residual concern: whether the new refusal path in MiMo/ModelLoading cleans up its reservations the same way as the cancellation path (the patch shows `throw interruption` after release, which looks equivalent). Human or integration review should confirm the truncated ModelLoading hunks.
